transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining. As you know, we have a non-final office action on our automated diagnostic platform patent application, and the response is due 28 days from today. Before we finalize our prosecution plan, I want to make sure we go through the pre-filing review properly. I need each of your areas -- patent prosecution, product, government contracts, and IP operations -- to report any issues that could affect this filing. Does anyone have anything to raise?

transcript.text: Elena, I need to raise an issue from patent prosecution. While preparing the office-action response, I completed a supplemental prior-art comparison that shows claims 1 through 6 are anticipated by the prior art. However, claim 7 remains patentable if we narrow the prosecution track to claim 7 only. I completed this comparison after the current response draft went to internal review, so it hasn't been circulated yet. This is significant because the current draft response continues pursuing the existing claim set, which based on my analysis would include claims that are anticipated. We should discuss whether to revise the response to focus on claim 7 before the 28-day deadline.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, I need to raise a product issue. I confirmed with the platform engineering team this week that our next commercial release depends on preserving the claim 12 improvement, which is not covered by the viable claim 7 that Theo just identified. The engineering team actually needs a continuation focused on the claim 12 improvement. This product requirement was recorded in a launch-planning file rather than the patent matter, so it hasn't been visible in the prosecution discussions. This is critical because if we narrow the response to claim 7 only and don't file a continuation for the claim 12 improvement, we risk losing IP coverage that the product roadmap depends on.

I verified against our federal research grant file that the invention used grant-funded work, which means the filing must include the exact government-funding notice required by the grant terms: 'This invention was made with Government support under Grant No. 12345 awarded by the National Institutes of Health.' I have not yet added this notice to the response checklist because the grant file was reviewed by government contracts rather than the patent group, so it hasn't been on the prosecution team's radar. transcript.text: Elena, I need to raise an IP operations issue. In reviewing the executed inventor records, I found that one inventor's assignment omits the continuation rights needed for this patent family. Before filing any continuation, the company must obtain and record a corrected assignment. I had not raised this earlier because the assignment repository is maintained separately from our docketing system, so it wasn't flagged in the normal prosecution workflow. This is directly relevant to Mina's point about needing a continuation for the claim 12 improvement -- we cannot file that continuation until the corrected assignment is secured and recorded.
